subject: Using plot_click to create a vector, then send values of vector to C program

messages.author: 3964139f80016e6d
messages.subject: Using plot_click to create a vector, then send values of vector to C program
parts:
Hi, I'll try to be clear about what I'd like to do.
I have a shiny app that displays a plot with what I'll call a base function (a semicircle) that does not change and a dynamic curve that is produced by a C program (a lagrangian interpolation program) that is called within the shiny app, which takes input parameters that are set using two slide bars.  One is an integer parameter ("anchors") indicating the number of anchor values (they are values that are randomly generated and lie on the semicircle; used to define the interpolation polynomial (lagrange polynomial), and the other is an integer parameter ("points") indicatign the number of values that are to be interpolated by the C program.
What I need to do is add functionality whereby clicking on the plot (created in ggplot) adds additional anchor values, and updates parameter values sent to the C program, resulting in an updated interpolation plot. 
I'm thinking that using  plot_click to produce a vector of values that will be used in issuing a new call to the C program.  Only x coordinate values would be needed for the C program to run.  (The Y coordinates are calculated in the C program from the x coordinates.)

My functioning shiny app is as follows (it is a bit more complex than I described, as there are multiple base functions that can be
switched using a radio button.

Oh, another note: The "name" variable that is used in the C function call is sort of a hack whereby the exact character strings produced by the radio button are used in order to call the relevant C program.  There is one C program for each of the base functions.  I know there is a better way to do this so that I don't have to render the text for the exact names of the C functions, but I couldn't figure it out.

Thanks for any help with this. 


library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

argv_graphtest3 <- function (name, points, anchors)
{
  name2 = paste("/home/matto/education/STC/finalproject/", name, sep="")
  tempfilename = paste("/home/matto/education/STC/finalproject/", name, "temporary.txt", sep="")
  file.create(tempfilename)
  command = paste(name2, points, anchors, ">", tempfilename)
  system(command)
  data = read.table(tempfilename,header=FALSE)
  return (data)
}

semicircle <- function(x) (25-x^2)^.5
non_polynomial <- function(x) 6 + 10*(x-2) - 8*(x+1)^3 + x^5
non_linear <- function(x) 6 + 10*(x-.2) - 8*(x+.1)^3 + x^5
#test2 <- function(x) 6 + 4*x-(9.8/6)*x^2 + (1/6)*x^3
test4 <- function(x) 6 + 10*x - 8*x^3 + x^5

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Lagrange Interpolation"),
  sidebarLayout(
  sidebarPanel(
  sliderInput(inputId = "num",
              label = "Choose anchor points",
              value = 5, min = 1, max = 50),
  sliderInput(inputId = "num2",
              label = "Choose interpolated points",
              value = 50, min = 1, max = 500),
  radioButtons("basefunction", "select base function",
               list("degree_5_polynomial", "semicircle", "semicircle_unanchored", "degree_5_nonlinear"), "")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("hist"), width = "100%")
)
  )

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$hist <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(argv_graphtest3(input$basefunction, input$num2, input$num),
           aes(x=V2, y=V3)) + geom_point(shape = 1) + geom_line(colour = "black") +
      stat_function(fun = test4, colour = "green") +
      stat_function(fun = non_linear, colour = "blue") +
      stat_function(fun = semicircle, colour = "red") + ylim (-10, 20) +
      coord_fixed(1) + xlim(-10,10)
   
    #    hist(rnorm(input$num))
  }, height = 700, width = 600)
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
